pharm: Multitargeted antifolate that, after intracellular polyglutamation, inhibits thymidylate synthase, dihydrofolate reductase and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase, disrupting de novo thymidine and purine synthesis required for cell replication.

summary: Pemetrexed is a folate-analog metabolic inhibitor used in non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (with pembrolizumab and platinum, with cisplatin, as maintenance, or after prior chemotherapy) and in malignant pleural mesothelioma with cisplatin. It is not used for squamous NSCLC. Mandatory folic acid and vitamin B12 supplementation reduce hematologic and GI toxicity, and it must not be given when creatinine clearance is below 45 mL/min.
indications: Initial treatment of metastatic non-squamous NSCLC (no EGFR/ALK aberrations) in combination with pembrolizumab and platinum chemotherapy
Initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC in combination with cisplatin
Maintenance treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC not progressed after four cycles of platinum-based first-line therapy (single agent)
Treatment of recurrent metastatic non-squamous NSCLC after prior chemotherapy (single agent)
Initial treatment of unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma in combination with cisplatin
Not indicated for squamous cell NSCLC

moa: Pemetrexed is a folate analog metabolic inhibitor. It enters cells via reduced folate carrier and folate-binding protein transport systems and is converted by folylpolyglutamate synthetase to polyglutamate forms that are retained intracellularly. These forms inhibit thymidylate synthase, dihydrofolate reductase and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase, disrupting folate-dependent de novo biosynthesis of thymidine and purine nucleotides and thereby halting DNA synthesis and cell replication.

absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity reaction to pemetrexed
relative: Creatinine clearance below 45 mL/min (do not administer)
Concurrent NSAIDs in patients with renal impairment

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data (fetal malformations and embryotoxicity). Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for a period after the last dose, and advise males with female partners to use contraception. Avoid in pregnancy unless benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child.
renal: Pemetrexed is primarily eliminated renally; clearance falls and exposure rises as renal function declines. Do not administer when creatinine clearance is below 45 mL/min, as severe and sometimes fatal renal failure can occur. Avoid concurrent NSAIDs around dosing in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: Reversible transaminase elevations can occur. Monitor liver function and apply dose modifications for severe hepatic toxicity per the prescribing information.

major: Nephrotoxic drugs (increase risk of severe/fatal renal failure)
moderate: NSAIDs - ibuprofen and other NSAIDs (reduce pemetrexed clearance, especially in renal impairment; hold around dosing)
Probenecid and other drugs cleared by tubular secretion
interactions.food: Not applicable (intravenous administration); folic acid supplementation is required.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatic and gastrointestinal burden.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC and renal function around each cycle.

serious: Severe myelosuppression with increased infection risk
Severe and sometimes fatal renal failure
emergency: Severe blistering or exfoliating skin reaction

missed: Pemetrexed is administered by a clinician on a fixed 21-day cycle. A missed or delayed dose is rescheduled by the oncology team; patients should not self-administer.
overdose: No approved antidote. Based on animal data, leucovorin may mitigate toxicity. It is not known whether pemetrexed is dialyzable. Provide supportive care and monitor blood counts and organ function.
